shots.script_excerpt: In 2016, Cláudia Carvalho’s team gave people with chronic low-back pain pills they were explicitly told had no active ingredient.
shots.intent: Open on the genuinely surprising fact with the primary paper as the evidence anchor.
shots.visual_reason: A paper-shaped hero visual grounds the hook in a real randomized trial while a clearly labeled capsule makes the disclosed-inert premise instantly legible.

label_requirements.paper_title: Open-label placebo treatment in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial
label_requirements.authors: Cláudia Carvalho, Joaquim Machado Caetano, Lidia Cunha, Paula Rebouta, Ted J. Kaptchuk, Irving Kirsch
label_requirements.institutions: ISPA; Nova Medical School; Hospital de Egas Moniz; Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center / Harvard Medical School
label_requirements.finding: Participants were told the pills had no active ingredient.

media.rendering: Native publication facsimile: first-page paper card, highlighted phrase 'open-label placebo,' oversized transparent capsule stamped 'NO ACTIVE INGREDIENT.'

publication.title: Open-label placebo treatment in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial
publication.finding: In a three-week randomized trial, open-label placebo added to treatment as usual was associated with larger reductions in self-reported chronic low-back-pain intensity and back-related disability than treatment as usual alone. The trial randomized 97 adults; 83 completed analysis. Its authors note that outcomes were subjective, the sample was small, and duration was too short for long-term clinical recommendations.

shots.intent: Let the presenter react before revealing the inversion.
shots.visual_reason: A tight host reaction with a giant capsule hovering at eye level creates a clean comedic pause.

label_requirements.host_expression: Genuinely baffled, as if the presenter has just lost an argument with a pill.
label_requirements.prop: Single plain white capsule, comically oversized.

shots.intent: Contrast open-label placebo with the familiar deceptive-placebo mental model.
shots.visual_reason: A tiny spy-movie capsule sneaking behind a curtain makes 'hidden' literal, then visibly fails at hiding.

label_requirements.generated_illustration_note: Illustrative gag only; not evidence of study procedure.
label_requirements.visual: Capsule in miniature sunglasses attempting to hide behind an obviously too-small curtain.

shots.intent: Land the central inversion with a deliberately theatrical reveal.
shots.visual_reason: A loudspeaker label on a plainly displayed capsule makes transparent disclosure feel startling rather than technical.

label_requirements.visual: Museum pedestal capsule with a tiny public-address microphone announcing itself.

media.rendering: Native typography plus generated prop illustration.

shots.script_excerpt: So what was delivered? Explanation. Timing. Repetition. Attention.
shots.intent: Visualize the contextual components without claiming any single one is proven causal.
shots.visual_reason: A single ritual-control panel turns the abstract list into an intelligible sequence: explanation card, clock cue, looping reminder, attentive check-in.

label_requirements.generated_illustration_note: Illustration of candidate contextual components, not proof that these are the causal mechanism.
label_requirements.source_context: Mechanisms of open-label placebo remain unconfirmed; framing, expectancy, conditioning, and context are candidate contributors.

media.rendering: Generated editorial illustration: one control panel with four large tactile controls, each represented by an icon rather than dense text.

shots.script_excerpt: The tiny ceremonial moment where care officially begins.
shots.intent: Make the ritual feel emotionally concrete.
shots.visual_reason: A mundane pill bottle receives an absurdly formal red-carpet arrival: velvet rope, miniature bell, and a hand pressing a ceremonial start button.

label_requirements.generated_illustration_note: Metaphor only; does not assert a tested mechanism.
label_requirements.focal_idea: A small routine can signal a beginning.

shots.script_excerpt: Maybe the pill is not the treatment.
shots.intent: Set up the reframe by demoting the capsule from medical hero to humble button.
shots.visual_reason: A capsule wearing an oversized doctor cape is gently relieved of it by a cursor hand.

shots.intent: State the thesis in one instantly graspable image.
shots.visual_reason: The capsule morphs into a large tactile 'START CARE' button on a friendly interface, preserving the pill silhouette as the visual thesis.

label_requirements.generated_illustration_note: Thesis metaphor only; no claim that pill effects are reducible to interface design.

media.rendering: Generated illustration with restrained native title typography.

shots.script_excerpt: A phone can explain a protocol, ring at the right time, repeat the rationale, and ask how you feel.
shots.intent: Show the phone carrying several ritual functions.
shots.visual_reason: A phone interface performs four simple actions in sequence: explainer card, reminder chime, recurring rationale, check-in slider—specific to the narration rather than generic wellness imagery.

label_requirements.generated_illustration_note: Phone actions are a conceptual demonstration of deliverable contextual components, not evidence of clinical equivalence.
label_requirements.source_context: A 20-day inert smartphone intervention manipulated expectancy and credibility through instructions and feedback.

media.rendering: Dynamic_broll illustrated phone sequence; no claims of symptom improvement displayed.

shots.intent: Draw a sharp boundary between digital context and pharmacology.
shots.visual_reason: A phone in a tiny lab coat tries to enter a molecular-model costume booth; the booth displays a polite red 'NOPE.'

label_requirements.generated_illustration_note: Comic boundary illustration; no medical claim beyond narration.

shots.script_excerpt: But it can be a very competent stage manager.
shots.intent: Pay off the interface idea with a visual role metaphor.
shots.visual_reason: The phone wears a headset backstage, cueing a clock, explanation card, and check-in spotlight while the capsule waits calmly onstage.

label_requirements.callback_asset: The capsule from sh09 appears as a non-hero prop.

shots.script_excerpt: Whether that digital ritual can reproduce a pill protocol’s effects is untested.
shots.intent: Mark the evidence boundary with the most relevant digital-placebo study.
shots.visual_reason: The study itself sits center frame, connected by a dotted bridge from phone to pill that stops before reaching the capsule: a precise visual for 'not yet tested.'

label_requirements.paper_title: Induction of Efficacy Expectancies in an Ambulatory Smartphone-Based Digital Placebo Mental Health Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial
label_requirements.authors: Esther Stalujanis, Joel Neufeld, Martina Glaus Stalder, Angelo Belardi, Marion Tegethoff, Gunther Meinlschmidt
label_requirements.institutions: University of Basel; International Psychoanalytic University Berlin; RWTH Aachen; University Hospital Basel
label_requirements.finding: In 132 healthy participants, an inert smartphone intervention manipulated expectancy and credibility; it did not demonstrate symptom improvement or equivalence to a pill protocol.

media.rendering: Native publication facsimile with a clearly unfinished dotted phone-to-pill bridge.

publication.title: Induction of Efficacy Expectancies in an Ambulatory Smartphone-Based Digital Placebo Mental Health Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial
publication.finding: A 20-day inert smartphone intervention in 132 healthy participants manipulated and measured credibility and efficacy expectancy through instructions and feedback. The reported endpoint was expectancy/credibility, not demonstrated symptom improvement in mood, stress, pain, or a clinical condition.
